paragraphs: Mentioned at the beginnings of Jerusalem Talmud Horayot, chapter 3, and Sanhedrin, chapter 2, reporting in the name of Rabbi Acha, in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish.[^1]

notes.text: רפ״ג and רפ״ב give beginnings of Horayot chapter 3 and Sanhedrin chapter 2, not ends; Jerusalem Talmud carries through the connected list. Guggenheimer Horayot 3:1 explicitly gives Rabbi Chanina Ketuva, Rabbi Acha, in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish, supporting all three full-title expansions. Named כתובא differs from supplied כתובה and does not replace it. The witness juxtaposes Chanina/Acha, whereas Hyman gives a sequential reporting chain; the English retains Hyman’s sequence and discloses the different attachment rather than merging them. The exact Sanhedrin locus is not independently checked.
